Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A study by researchers at the National Institute of Mental Health's (NIMH) Emotion and Development Branch, published online on October 18, 2023, established that exposure-based cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a viable and promising treatment for children with severe irritability and temper outbursts. The research, which involved 40 participants aged 8-17, tested a novel, manual-based CBT that integrates parent management skills. Results showed significant improvement in irritability symptoms, with no participants dropping out of the treatment phase and no adverse events reported, supporting the therapy's acceptability and feasibility. By the end of the treatment, 65% of patients were considered significantly improved or recovered. The findings lay the groundwork for future, larger-scale clinical trials to further refine this therapeutic approach for youth with severe irritability, a core symptom of Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder (DMDD). <2> The American Psychological Association (APA) and ecoAmerica jointly released a report titled 'Mental Health and Our Changing Climate: Children and Youth Report 2023' on October 11, 2023. This report, a follow-up to a 2021 publication, synthesizes research on the significant mental health impacts of climate change on children and youth, from prenatal development onward. It highlights that climate-related factors, such as extreme weather events, heat, and air pollution, can interrupt fetal development and increase the risk for anxiety, depression, PTSD, and developmental issues. The report states that these effects are compounded by other societal stressors like racism, poverty, and housing insecurity, which disproportionately affect certain populations. It serves as a resource for various stakeholders, including health professionals, policymakers, and educators, offering guidance and solutions to mitigate these harmful impacts at individual, community, and systemic levels. <3> The 'Targeting Emotional and Mental Stability (TEAMS) Act of 2023' (S.2966) was introduced in the U.S. Senate on September 28, 2023, by Senators John Boozman (R-AR) and Cory Booker (D-NJ), both former college football players. The bipartisan bill aims to amend the Public Health Service Act to make school-based initiatives that support the mental health of college athletes eligible for the Garrett Lee Smith (GLS) Campus Suicide Prevention Grant Program. This is intended to improve access to mental health resources and support services, addressing survey findings from the NCAA that show elevated levels of mental exhaustion, anxiety, and depression among student-athletes. The act would allow grant funding to be used for services such as direct mental health care, peer-to-peer counseling, crisis lines, and training for staff on responding to students in mental distress. A companion bill, H.R.5901, was introduced in the House of Representatives on October 6, 2023. <4> The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Exxua (gepirone extended-release), a new treatment for adults with major depressive disorder (MDD), on September 22, 2023. [6] The approval was announced by the manufacturer, Fabre-Kramer Pharmaceuticals, on September 28, 2023. [2] Exxua is considered a new class of antidepressant, being the first and only approved medication that selectively targets the serotonin 1A receptor, a key regulator of mood. [2] This novel mechanism of action distinguishes it from other available treatments. Clinical trials involving over 5,000 patients demonstrated Exxua's effectiveness in relieving depressive symptoms with an acceptable side effect profile; notably, the approved labeling does not list sexual dysfunction or weight gain as adverse reactions, and the most common side effects were mild dizziness and nausea. [2, 4] The drug was expected to become available in pharmacies in early 2024. [2, 3] <5> Grammy-winning rapper Megan Thee Stallion partnered with the 'Seize the Awkward' campaign for a public service announcement (PSA) titled "Check In On Your Friends," which launched on September 26, 2023. [1, 2, 3, 7] In the PSA, she discusses the pressure to always appear strong and encourages young people to be vulnerable and check in on their friends' mental health, emphasizing that 'It's OK to not be OK.' [1, 7, 9] The 'Seize the Awkward' campaign is a joint effort by the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP) and The Jed Foundation (JED), in collaboration with the Ad Council, aimed at inspiring young adults, particularly Black and Hispanic youth, to have conversations about mental health. [1, 4, 5, 8] The initiative also promoted Megan Thee Stallion's own mental health resource website, 'BadBitchesHaveBadDaysToo.com'. [1, 4, 7] The campaign was developed pro bono by the creative agency Droga5. [1, 2, 4, 5] <6> A research initiative by the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH), known as Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode (RAISE), has been recognized for its transformative impact on the mental health landscape in the United States. [1] Launched in June 2008, the RAISE initiative was designed to test and implement coordinated specialty care (CSC) for individuals experiencing their first episode of psychosis. [1, 2] The success of the program has inspired what NIMH describes as a "revolution in treating schizophrenia," leading to the rapid growth of CSC programs across the nation and providing increased access to high-quality, recovery-oriented care for thousands of Americans. [1, 5] Research from the initiative demonstrated that CSC treatment improved patients' quality of life, symptoms, and engagement with work and school. [1] <7> On August 23, 2023, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) announced awards of more than $64 million to address the nation's mental health crisis, with the news being published the following day. This funding, made available through the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act signed by President Biden, includes $59.4 million for states and territories via the Community Mental Health Services Block Grant (MHBG) program. The initiative aims to fortify the public mental health system, assist individuals experiencing a crisis, and support those in long-term recovery. <8> Dr. Patricia A. Areán, Ph.D., was selected as the new director of the National Institute of Mental Health's (NIMH) Division of Services and Intervention Research (DSIR), beginning her role on August 13, 2023. [2] The announcement was made by the NIMH on August 14, 2023. [2, 3] Dr. Areán, who was previously at the University of Washington, now leads the funding for major national scientific research programs and oversees policy and procedural issues for NIMH's extramural intervention and services research. [2, 4] She has over 30 years of experience in mental health services and intervention research and founded the CREATIV Lab at the University of Washington. [2, 4] <9> On August 11, 2023, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), announced over $88 million in grants to enhance school-based mental health programs and broaden access to treatments for substance use disorders. The largest portion of this funding, $42.2 million, was designated for Project Advancing Wellness and Resiliency in Education (AWARE), aimed at developing a sustainable infrastructure for mental health services in schools. Additional awards included $17.5 million for the National Child Traumatic Stress Initiative and $15.3 million for Grants for the Benefit of Homeless Individuals, among others. This initiative is part of the Biden-Harris Administration's focus on addressing the nation's mental health crisis. <10> Selena Gomez hosted the inaugural Rare Impact Fund Benefit, titled 'A Night of Radiance & Reflection', on October 4, 2023, at Nya Studios in Los Angeles. The event was established to support the Rare Impact Fund's mission to reduce the stigma surrounding mental illness and increase young people's access to mental health services and education globally. The benefit was emceed by Gomez's "Only Murders in the Building" co-star, Martin Short, and featured a special performance by H.E.R. and a DJ set by Marshmello. All proceeds from the evening, including a live auction, were directed to the fund, which supports 23 organizations worldwide.

[5, 7] This partnership is an extension of the Ad Council's national "Love, Your Mind" campaign and its "The Rituals We Share" series, which aims to encourage a more open and proactive approach to mental health. Blank Family Foundation announced grants exceeding $2 million designated for six national and local nonprofit organizations in Georgia and Montana. The FDA did not request any new clinical trials and did not express concerns about the stability of the ketamine submission batches. This decision delays the potential relief for a national ketamine shortage that has been ongoing since February 2018. PharmaTher stated it would work with its manufacturing partner to address the deficiencies promptly. Prediction target period: from 2025-08-03 to 2025-10-19. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On July 24, 2025, the White House released an Executive Order titled “Ending Crime and Disorder on America’s Streets,” which directs federal agencies to make it easier to involuntarily treat individuals with serious mental illnesses in an effort to address homelessness. [1] The following day, the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) issued a statement expressing grave concerns, arguing that the order promotes the institutionalization of people with mental illness. [1] <2> On July 24, 2025, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) voted to require all wireless carriers to implement georouting for text messages sent to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. [5, 6] This measure is designed to improve crisis response by routing texts based on the user's geographic location rather than their phone's area code, thereby connecting them to the nearest local crisis center for more immediate and relevant support. [1, 5] The new rule follows a similar mandate for 988 voice calls that the FCC issued in the fall of 2024. [4, 5] To implement the change, nationwide wireless providers have 18 months, while non-nationwide providers are given 36 months. [1, 5] The FCC has also addressed privacy concerns, requiring that the location data used for routing be aggregated to avoid identifying the precise location of the person sending the text. [1] The decision was formally announced in a statement from the FCC on July 25, 2025. [2] <3> On June 27, 2025, the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) issued a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for organizations. [1] This initiative aims to fund the implementation of targeted strategies to improve treatment and services for individuals with substance use disorder (SUD) and/or co-occurring substance misuse and mental disorders (COD). [1] The deadline for applications was July 15, 2025. [1] <4> On the third anniversary of the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline on July 16, 2025, the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) released a new poll conducted with Ipsos. [4, 5, 10] The poll revealed that awareness of the 988 hotline has reached an all-time high, with 74% of Americans having heard of it, a significant increase from 44% in September 2022. [4, 5] Despite this success, the findings highlight a broad dissatisfaction with the current state of mental health care in the U.S., with 73% of Americans stating they are not content. [5, 9] The poll also indicated strong public support for increased government funding for 988 and associated crisis response services, with 86% believing it should be a congressional priority. [5, 8] <5> On July 10, 2025, the United Way of Greater Milwaukee & Waukesha County announced the 2025-26 grantees for its Mental Health Improvement Fund. This fund, previously known as the Health Improvement Fund, supports organizations that deliver mental and behavioral health services to low-income and underserved youth and adult populations in Milwaukee County. The initiative aims to enhance access to mental health care, improve outcomes, and foster health equity. The 2025-26 funding cycle focuses on programs providing early identification and intervention, outpatient treatment, crisis intervention, and care coordination for mental health and substance use. Grantees for this cycle include Advocate Aurora Walker's Point Community Clinic, Ascension Wisconsin Foundation, the Benedict Center, and Pathfinders, among others. <6> The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted Breakthrough Therapy designation to TSND-201 (methylone) for the treatment of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), Transcend Therapeutics announced on July 10, 2025. [1] This designation, intended to expedite the development of promising drugs for serious conditions, was based on positive results from the Phase 2 IMPACT-1 clinical trial. [3, 5] The trial, which enrolled 65 patients with severe PTSD, showed that TSND-201 led to rapid, robust, and durable symptom improvement compared to a placebo. [2, 5] Statistically significant improvements were observed as early as day 10 and were sustained through day 64. [1, 4] TSND-201 is described as a rapid-acting neuroplastogen and a proprietary formulation of methylone that is non-hallucinogenic, as it primarily acts on monoamine transporters with no activity at the 5HT-2a receptor. [1, 3, 5] The treatment was well-tolerated, with no hallucinations reported. [3, 4] <7> On July 8, 2025, Governor Kathy Hochul announced that new network adequacy regulations took effect in New York on July 1, 2025. These rules mandate that individuals with qualifying health insurance plans, specifically Medicaid Managed Care, Child Health Plus, and the Essential Plan, must be given access to an initial outpatient appointment for behavioral health care within 10 business days of their request. <8> On June 21, 2025, Phase 1 Labs announced the upcoming launch of 'Phase 2,' a new electronic patient software. The software is scheduled to become available starting July 1, 2025. It is specifically designed for the mental healthcare industry and aims to reduce screen time for professionals, allowing them to remain more present with clients. Key features of the software include smart automation and voice-to-text tools to streamline documentation and workflows. <9> The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) announced in June 2025 that the specialized service line for LGBTQ+ youth, accessed by pressing '3' on the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, would be terminated. The service officially ended on July 17, 2025. SAMHSA, an agency within the Trump administration, stated the closure was due to the exhaustion of $33 million in congressionally directed funding, which had been fully spent by June 2025. A spokesperson claimed that continuing the service would have required reallocating funds from the main 988 lifeline, thereby compromising the entire system. However, critics, including a former senior adviser at SAMHSA and advocacy groups like The Trevor Project, which was a primary service provider for the line, argue the decision was politically motivated and aligns with the administration's efforts to dismantle diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. Opponents also noted the administration's announcement referred to "LGB+ youth services," omitting the 'T' for transgender, which they called callous and an erasure. The Trevor Project reported it received official notice of the program's end on June 17, 2025, and that the closure resulted in the loss of a $25 million federal contract and the layoff of over 200 counselors. <10> The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) announced the elimination of specialized services for LGBTQ+ youth within the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, effective July 17, 2025. [2, 6, 7] This service, known as the 'Press 3' option, connected young people with trained counselors, many with lived experience, to provide tailored support. [2] The announcement, made in June 2025 during Pride Month, has drawn significant concern and criticism from mental health advocacy groups like NAMI, The Trevor Project, and the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP). [2, 3, 6, 9] These organizations highlight that LGBTQ+ youth are more than four times as likely to attempt suicide than their peers and that the specialized line served nearly 1.3 million contacts since its pilot launch in late 2022. [2] SAMHSA stated the change was made to 'focus on serving all help seekers' and cited that congressionally directed funding for the third-party-managed service had been depleted. [5, 10] Critics, however, have questioned the funding explanation, suggesting the decision was a politically motivated move to dismantle diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives. [9] While SAMHSA assures that all callers to 988 will continue to receive competent care, advocates worry that the loss of this specialized, trusted pathway could lead to tragic outcomes and deter at-risk youth from seeking help. [5, 9, 12]
